reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure, let (Omega,mu) be a probability space, and let iota be a finite type of nodes. Let V:E->R be twice continuously Frechet differentiable and let kappa>=1 satisfy (1/kappa)||v||^2 <= D^2V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2 for every x,v in E. Let 0<eta<=c<1 and eps>0. Let X,P:Omega->E be measurable, let xstar in E satisfy grad V(xstar)=0, and suppose w |-> ||X(w)-xstar||^2+||P(w)||^2 is integrable with expectation at most M. For each i in iota let t_i be real with |t_i|<=1, set Y0_i=X+t_i P, and let G_j:Omega->E be measurable innovations such that ||G_j||^2 is integrable with expectation at most dim_R(E) for every j. Let real weights omega_ij satisfy sum_j |omega_ij|<=S for every i, and define B=6M+3eps^2+3eta dim_R(E). Then there exist measurable functions p:E->E, N:E->N, and q:E->E such that, for every y in E, p(y)+eta grad V(p(y))=y, ||q(y)-p(y)||<=eps, and the finite exact-real proximalQuery run on y with fuel N(y)+1 returns some(q(y),N(y)+1), where the recorded natural number counts all gradient tests including the successful one. Define Z0_j=grad V(q(Y0_j)+sqrt(eta)G_j) and Y1_i=Y0_i-sum_j omega_ij Z0_j, pointwise on Omega. Then, for every applicable node index, each of ||grad V(Y0_i)||^2, ||Z0_j||^2, and ||grad V(Y1_i)||^2 is integrable, and their expectations satisfy E_mu||grad V(Y0_i)||^2<=2M, E_mu||Z0_j||^2<=B, and E_mu||grad V(Y1_i)||^2<=4M+2S^2B.
objects: The ambient space E; probability space (Omega,mu); finite node type iota; potential V, gradient, and Hessian; scalars kappa, eta, c, eps, M, and S; stationary point xstar; measurable random variables X and P; nodes t_i; innovations G_j; weights omega_ij; initial random positions Y0_i; the moment constant B; measurable proximal witnesses p, N, and q; transformed gradients Z0_j; and updated random positions Y1_i.
domains: E is a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure. Omega carries a probability measure mu. The index type iota is finite. V:E->R, X,P,G_j:Omega->E, xstar in E, t_i and omega_ij in R, p,q:E->E, and N:E->N. The real dimension finrank(E) is coerced to R in moment bounds. Expectations are real Bochner integrals with respect to mu.
quantifiers: The theorem is universal over the ambient spaces and structures, finite node type, V, kappa, eta, c, eps, the probability measure, X, P, xstar, M, the node family t, innovation family G, weight family omega, and S, subject to the assumptions. Hessian bounds hold for all x,v in E; node and row-sum conditions hold for every node i; innovation conditions hold for every j. It then existentially chooses deterministic measurable p, N, and q. Their proximal properties hold for every y in E, while the three integrability claims and inequalities hold for every applicable i or j.
assumptions: V is C^2; kappa>=1; and (1/kappa)||v||^2 <= D^2V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2 for all x,v. The parameters satisfy 0<eta<=c<1 and eps>0. X and P are measurable; grad V(xstar)=0; and ||X-xstar||^2+||P||^2 is integrable with expectation at most M. Each node obeys |t_i|<=1. Every G_j is measurable, ||G_j||^2 is integrable, and E_mu||G_j||^2<=dim_R(E). Every weight row obeys sum_j|omega_ij|<=S. No independence or Gaussian-law assumption is made.
conclusion: There exist measurable p, N, and q giving, pointwise in y, an exact proximal fixed point p(y), an eps-accurate returned point q(y), and a successful finite proximalQuery result whose recorded cost is N(y)+1 gradient tests. With Z0 and Y1 defined from these witnesses, all three displayed squared-gradient random variables are integrable and satisfy the bounds 2M, B, and 4M+2S^2B, respectively.
scopes: Y0_i=X+t_iP is defined before the existential witnesses and is pointwise on Omega. B=6M+3eps^2+3eta dim_R(E) is in scope for the Z0 bound and final Y1 bound. The functions p, N, and q are functions on E, not random functions of w; their pointwise proximal and interpreter assertions are under 'for every y'. After choosing them, Z0_j and then Y1_i are defined pointwise, with the finite sum ranging over all j in iota. Integrability is asserted separately before each expectation inequality is used.
constant_dependencies: B=6M+3eps^2+3eta dim_R(E) depends only on M, eps, eta, and the real dimension of E. The initial gradient bound is 2M. The innovation-transformed bound is B. The updated gradient bound 4M+2S^2B additionally depends on the row-sum control S. These displayed moment constants have no explicit dependence on kappa, c, the number of nodes, the individual t_i, the individual weights, or the laws and dependence structure of the innovations beyond the stated marginal moment and row-sum bounds. The witnesses p, N, and q may depend on V, kappa, eta, c, eps, and the ambient structures, but not on the realization w.
